summary.text: Pamela Hornberger is the Republican candidate for Michigan House of Representatives District 63 in the November 3, 2026 general election and a former Republican state representative who represented District 32 from January 1, 2017, to January 1, 2023.
She was selected to replace Jay DeBoyer on the general election ballot after DeBoyer was chosen as the running mate for the Republican gubernatorial candidate.

paragraphs.text: Pamela Hornberger won an at-large seat on the L'Anse Creuse Public Schools board in the 2010 election and served on it from 2010 to 2016.
She took office in the Michigan House of Representatives, representing District 32, on January 1, 2017, and won re-election in 2018 over Democrat Paul Manley.
In the 2019-2020 term, Hornberger was assigned to the Education Committee, which she chaired, along with the Health Policy and Elections and Ethics committees.
In 2021-2022 she again chaired the Education Committee and also served on the House Appropriations Committee.
Rather than seek re-election to the House in 2022, she ran for Michigan State Senate District 12 and lost the general election to Democrat Kevin Hertel, 50.2% to 49.8%.
